messages:
Alex: Quick ask — can someone grab a small nsys capture for model-resnet-lm v2 (batch=1, seq=512) on rtx-6000-test? Need ~30s steady-state after KV warmup. This will be a lightweight smoke run for a flamegraph compare.

Maria: I can do it. Do you want the raw qdrep or an exported sqlite + flamegraph SVG? Also any scrub rules? :mag:

Alex: Raw qdrep is fine, but please keep under 60MB if possible. Scrub hostnames + any customer prompt text. No credential blobs. If easier, upload qdrep to s3://redwood-profiling/tmp/ and PerfBot will export for us.

Sam: I've got a free slot on that node at 10:30 PST, I can run it then. What's the exact command you want?

Alex: Thanks Sam. Rough command we use for quick runs:
```
nsys profile --output=trace_resnetlm_quick --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --sample=none \
  --duration=30 --capture-range=cpuopprof python -u run_infer.py \
  --model resnet-lm-v2 --batch 1 --seq_len 512 --prefill_kv 1
```
Add `--prefill_kv 1` so the KV warmup happens before capture.

Jin: Note: use `--sample=none` for deterministic call stacks, but that makes larger files. If it hits >60MB, switch to `--sample=cpu` and add `--sampling-rate=1000`. Also please mount `/tmp` to ephemeral storage to avoid filling home.

Leo: On scrub rules: run this before upload to strip hostnames and any env vars: 
```bash
# remove host metadata from qdrep after capture (quick export)
nsys export --input trace_resnetlm_quick.qdrep --output trace.sqlite --type=sqlite
sqlite3 trace.sqlite "DELETE FROM metadata WHERE key='hostname' OR key LIKE 'env_%';"
zip -9 trace_redacted.zip trace.sqlite
```
This keeps size down.

Sam: OK running at 10:30 PST. I'll upload to s3://redwood-profiling/tmp/trace_resnetlm_quick_2159876543.zip and ping here when done.

PerfBot: Upload helper — remember to add tag `team:eng-runtime` when you put it to S3 so the pipeline picks it up. Use `aws s3 cp --acl bucket-owner-full-control` if needed.

Sam: Uploaded. s3://redwood-profiling/tmp/trace_resnetlm_quick_2159876543.zip (36MB). PerfBot, can you kick the conversion? :pray:

PerfBot: Received artifact. Starting export -> flamegraph job. Estimated time ~45s. Job id: pf-8793.

PerfBot: Done. Outputs: s3://redwood-profiling/exports/pf-8793/trace_resnetlm_quick.qdrep, flamegraph at s3://redwood-profiling/exports/pf-8793/flame_resnetlm_v2.svg (30MB).

Maria: Can someone sanity-check the flamegraph for big kernels? I care about attention matmul and KV memory copy hotspots.

Alex: Opening the SVG now. Looks like a spike in `attention::matmul` around 12s and heavy `cudaMemcpyAsync` at 6s — probably the KV prefill. Jin, any red flags?

Jin: That pattern is expected with the current prefetcher. If the memcpy dominates steady-state tokens, we might need to tweak prefetch window. But from a 30s run it looks fine.

Leo: Quick follow-up: for future captures, please add `--nvtx-api` to include NVTX ranges from the runtime. Makes attribution easier.

Alex: Good call. Closing the loop — thanks @Sam for running and @PerfBot for the export. I'll attach the flamegraph to the bug and add a short note about KV prefetch. :white_check_mark:

Sam: np, happy to run again if you want a longer/parallel run.

Maria: Saved the flamegraph to the perf doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/perf/resnetlm/v2/2159876543.

Alex: Perfect. If someone wants the qdrep for deep dive, DM me and I'll give access to the S3 path.

PerfBot: Reminder: traces older than 90 days are auto-archived. Tag any long-term ones with `keep:true` if needed.
